skill.name: Bare claim or backed-up claim
skill.why: Anyone can say anything. A backed-up claim gives you something to check.
skill.how: Find the claim. Then look for a reason or proof holding it up.

steps.say: My slime is the stretchiest ever! Why believe me?

show.text: Gus's slime is the stretchiest ever.
show.nudge: That's what Gus wants you to believe. Which part shows why?

show.text: It stretched four metres in our test.

show.nudge: Telling you to buy isn't a reason to believe it. Which part shows why?

steps.ask: Tap the part that shows why you should believe Gus.
steps.win: Yes! The test is backing. It holds up Gus's claim.

show.text: Mo's pies are the best on Bluster Rock.

steps.ask: Does anything back up Mo's claim?

check.nudge: 'Buy one now!' tells you what to do. Does it show the pies are the best?

steps.win: Right! Nothing holds it up. That's a bare claim.

steps.say: Careful! Mo added a 'because'. Does that fix it?
show: because they are better than every other pie.

options.text: It gives proof.
options.reason: Say 'better than every other pie'. Now say 'the best'. Do they mean the same?

options.text: It tells you where to buy one.
options.reason: There's no shop or price here. Read the because part again.

options.text: It says the claim again.

steps.win: Yes! It just says 'the best' twice. That isn't backing.

steps.say: This 'because' is true. Mo's pies really are round.

options.text: Nothing. It's good backing.
options.reason: Lots of pies are round. Does being round make a pie the best?

options.text: It doesn't fit the claim.
It isn't true.
options.reason: Mo's pies really are round. Being true isn't enough. Does round show they're the best?

steps.win: Yes! Round doesn't make pies best. Backing must show why.

steps.say: Zed wants more library comics. Check his reasons.

show.nudge: 'Coolest' is only Zed's feeling. Does it show the library needs more?

show.text: Every comic in the library is borrowed right now.

show.nudge: Loving comics is a feeling. Which reason shows a real need?

steps.ask: Tap the reason that really backs up Zed's claim.
steps.win: Yes! Every comic is out. Feelings don't hold a claim up.

steps.say: Vinnie's robot cat: three claims. Check each reason.

show.text: It's quiet. It hums softer than a fridge.
show.nudge: Humming softer than a fridge shows it is quiet. Try another.

show.text: It's the best pet. It comes in blue.
It's cheap. It costs $5 less than others.
show.nudge: Costing less than the others shows it is cheap. Try another.

steps.ask: Tap the claim that is still bare.
steps.win: Yes! Blue doesn't show it's the best. That claim is bare.

terms.means: What the writer wants you to believe.
A reason or proof that shows why the claim is true.
A claim with nothing holding it up.
A claim with backing that fits it.

examples.text: Gus's slime is the stretchiest ever.
It stretched four metres in our test.

card.test: Find the claim. Does a reason or proof that fits hold it up? Yes: backed-up. No: bare.

weDo.hint: Which one gives you something you could check?
weDo.success: The four-metre test holds the claim up. The others just say it again, or tell you to buy.

options.text: Gus's slime is the stretchiest ever. Seriously, it is!
options.reason: 'Seriously, it is!' just says the claim again. Nothing holds it up.

options.text: Gus's slime is the stretchiest ever. It stretched four metres in our test.
Gus's slime is the stretchiest ever. Buy some today!
options.reason: Telling you to buy isn't a reason to believe it. The claim is bare.

weDo.prompt: Tap the sentence that backs up Tully's claim.
weDo.hint: Which sentence gives you a reason to believe her?
weDo.success: Winning all twelve games so far is proof the team is good. That backs up her claim.

parts: TULLY: The Reef Rays will win the cup this year.

parts.tap: They are the best team, full stop.
parts.reason: This just says the claim another way. It doesn't show why.

parts.tap: They have won all twelve games so far.
Go Rays!
parts.reason: A cheer isn't a reason. It doesn't back anything up.

write.ask: Back up Tully's bare claim. Add a reason or proof that fits it.
given: The Reef Rays are the best team in the league.
write.starter: The Reef Rays are the best team in the league, because
checks: I added a reason or proof someone could check.
My reason shows why the claim is true.
write.model: The Reef Rays are the best team in the league, because they have won all twelve games this season.

creature.name: Bilbolster
creature.blurb: A bilby whose huge ears prick up at every 'because'. A claim with nothing holding it up makes its ears flop.

encounters.frame: Three posters are up for the canteen vote. The Bilbolster's ears are twitching.
encounters.text: VOTE FOR NEXT TERM'S LUNCH SPECIAL! Poster 1: Vote for sushi! Sushi is the best lunch. This poster has 5 sushi stickers on it! Poster 2: Vote for wraps! Wraps are the best lunch. Last term, the canteen sold 300 wraps. It only sold 40 sushi rolls. Poster 3: Vote for pies! Pies are the best lunch. Vote pies, or Mo will be very sad. Voting closes on Friday. Put your vote in the box by the canteen door.
encounters.prompt: Which poster backs up its claim?
encounters.success: Poster 2 gives proof: lots more kids bought wraps. That holds its claim up.

options.text: Poster 1, for sushi
options.reason: Five stickers on a poster don't show sushi is the best lunch. The claim is bare.

options.text: Poster 2, for wraps
Poster 3, for pies
options.reason: Mo being sad doesn't show pies are the best lunch. The claim is bare.

I love bilbies more than anything.

encounters.frame: Tully has written a post for her footy blog. The Bilbolster is sorting her claims.
encounters.text: TULLY'S FOOTY BLOG. Hi, footy fans! Today I want to talk about my team, the Reef Rays. The Reef Rays are the best. They won the last three cups. Our coach is great. She has won Coach of the Year twice. Some people say netball is better than footy. They are wrong. Footy is the best sport. It just is. Our next game is on Saturday at 2 pm. Saturday's game will be the best one ever. Go Rays! See you there.
encounters.prompt: Put each of Tully's claims in the right box.
encounters.success: Cups and awards are proof, so those claims are backed up. A start time and 'It just is' aren't.

bins: backed-up claim: a reason or proof that supports it

items.text: The Reef Rays are the best. They won the last three cups.
items.reason: Three cups in a row is proof. That backs up the claim.

items.text: Saturday's game will be the best one ever. It starts at 2 pm.
items.reason: A start time doesn't show the game will be the best. The claim is bare.

items.text: Footy is the best sport. It just is.
items.reason: 'It just is' gives no reason. The claim is bare.

items.text: Our coach is great. She has won Coach of the Year twice.
items.reason: Two awards are proof she's a good coach. The claim is backed up.

encounters.prompt: Tap the reason that doesn't back up Zed's claim. Then choose a real one.
encounters.success: Forty kids wanting to join is a real reason. 'Really cool' is only Zed's feeling. It gives no proof.

parts: , and because

parts.reason: That's a real reason. It shows the club could happen.

encounters.frame: Maxx is showing off his rocket. The Bilbolster is hiding behind a cactus.
encounters.text: Maxx it out, Vantafam! Here she is, my Gold Rocket! Next week I'm flying her to the Moon. My rocket has a waterslide and a gold toilet. Some of you are worried. encounters.prompt: Maxx claims his rocket is safe. Which sentence would back up his claim?
encounters.success: Passing safety tests is proof. That would hold up the claim, if it's true.

options.text: It is super, super safe.
options.reason: This just says the claim again, louder. It isn't proof.

options.text: It is fifty metres tall and painted shiny gold.
options.reason: Being tall and gold doesn't make a rocket safe. It doesn't back up the claim.

parts.reason: Listening to all those stats is proof. This claim is backed up.

I'm helpful, because I clean the class fish tank every Friday.

parts.reason: Holding a python is proof he's brave. This claim is backed up.

parts: Vote for me! Why did the class captain bring a ladder? To take the class to new heights!

encounters.frame: Letters about the school band have flooded the Bluster Rock Bugle. The Bilbolster is reading them all.
encounters.text: This week, the Bugle asked readers about the Bluster Rock Primary school band. Should it get more money from the council? Here are some of the claims readers sent in. Some readers gave reasons. Others just said what they thought, and then said it again. One reader sent in a drawing of a trombone, which we have not printed. Last year, the band played at the Bluster Rock Show, the town's birthday picnic and the opening of the new skate park. The council will decide next month. Until then, the band will keep practising in the old shed behind the oval, where the roof leaks every time it rains.
encounters.prompt: Put each reader's claim in the right box.
encounters.success: Backed-up claims give proof that fits the claim. Bare claims repeat themselves, give orders, or add facts that don't fit.

bins: backed-up claim: a reason or proof that supports it

items.text: The band deserves more money. It won the state band competition this year.
items.reason: Winning the state competition is proof the band is worth it.

items.text: The band needs new instruments. Half the trumpets have holes in them.
items.reason: Trumpets with holes are proof they need replacing.

items.text: The band is fantastic. It has 24 players in red jackets.
items.reason: How many players it has and what they wear don't show it's fantastic. The claim is bare.

items.text: The council must give the band more money. Do it now!
items.reason: 'Do it now!' is an order, not a reason. The claim is bare.

items.text: The band brings people together. Over 500 people came to its last concert.
items.reason: A crowd of 500 is proof that the band brings people together.

encounters.frame: Maxx is selling rides on his jet ski. The Bilbolster has its ears up, waiting for proof.
encounters.text: Maxx it out, Vantafam! Today I'm at Bluster Bay with my gold jet ski, the Gold Rush. For one week only, you can win a ride on it! Just buy a Maxx Splash Pack from the Vantamart. I've written three ads for the Gold Rush, and my team can't decide which one to use. Ad 1: The Gold Rush is the fastest jet ski in the world. Nothing on the water is faster, not even a speedboat. NOTHING! Ad 2: The Gold Rush is the fastest jet ski in the world. It is covered in three kilograms of real gold. Ad 3: The Gold Rush is the fastest jet ski in the world. It won the Bluster Bay Race by two minutes. Help me choose, Vantafam. Comment your favourite below! Stay gold!
encounters.prompt: Which of Maxx's ads backs up its claim?
encounters.success: Winning the race by two minutes is proof of speed. That holds the claim up.

options.text: Ad 1
options.reason: 'Nothing is faster' says the same claim again, in capitals. Louder isn't proof.

options.text: Ad 2
options.reason: Gold doesn't make it fast. That fact doesn't hold up the claim.

options.text: Ad 3

encounters.frame: Indi wants an art room for Bluster Rock Primary. One of her reasons isn't pulling its weight.
encounters.text: At the moment, Bluster Rock Primary has no art room. Students paint at their desks, and there is nowhere to dry their work. Last term, Indi's papier-mâché galah was squashed under a pile of maths books. Mr Pettigrew is the caretaker. He says the storeroom is mostly full of broken chairs and one very old cricket bat. Indi has already drawn a plan of the room. It has easels by the windows and a drying rack along the back wall. She is writing a speech for the school council. Her plan is to turn the old storeroom next to the library into an art room. She has three reasons, but one of them only says her claim again. Help her fix it before Friday's meeting.
encounters.prompt: Tap the reason that doesn't back up Indi's claim. Then choose a real one.
encounters.success: Squashed paintings show a real problem an art room would fix. 'An art room is needed' just repeats the claim.

parts.reason: That's a real reason. It shows a problem an art room would fix.

parts.reason: That's a real reason. It shows the storeroom would work well.

we really, truly need one

encounters.frame: Slick Vinnie is selling robot dogs. The Bilbolster is checking his sign.
encounters.text: SLICK VINNIE'S ROBO-PUP! Ladies, gentlemen and lizards, meet the Robo-Pup, the robot dog that never needs a walk. It wags its tail, fetches the paper and barks at strangers. It costs $80 and comes with a spare tail. Vinnie has only twelve left, and he says they are 'going like hot pies'. Here are the three claims on his sign. Claim 1: The Robo-Pup is tough. It survived being dropped off the roof of the Vantamart. Claim 2: The Robo-Pup is the best robot dog. It is about the size of a small cat. Claim 3: The Robo-Pup is easy to look after. It only needs charging once a week. Vinnie's own Robo-Pup, Bolt Junior, has been wagging at everyone who walks past his stall all week.
encounters.prompt: Which claim on Vinnie's sign is bare?
encounters.success: Being the size of a cat doesn't show it's the best. The other two claims each have backing.

options.text: Claim 1, that it's tough
options.reason: Surviving a fall off a roof is proof it's tough. This claim is backed up.

options.text: Claim 2, that it's the best robot dog
Claim 3, that it's easy to look after
options.reason: Charging once a week is a reason it's easy. This claim is backed up.

parts.reason: The moaning wind is a reason the mine is spooky. This claim is backed up.

encounters.frame: Coach Dev Marsh is writing to the Bluster Rock Bugle. The Bilbolster is checking his draft for backing.
encounters.prompt: Dev claims the oval needs lights. Tap the sentence that really backs up his claim.
encounters.success: Barely an hour before dark shows a real problem. Backing doesn't need 'because', and 'because' doesn't make backing.

parts: Dear Editor, I coach the Bluster Rock Roos, our town's junior footy team. I am writing to ask the council to put lights on the oval at Red Dune Park.

parts.tap: I have coached at Red Dune Park for eleven years, longer than anyone else in town.
parts.reason: Eleven years tells you about Dev, not about the oval. It doesn't show lights are needed.

parts.tap: Every winter, the sun sets before 5:30 pm, so the kids get barely an hour of training before dark.
We need lights, because our kids deserve the very best.
parts.reason: 'Deserve the very best' is a feeling. It doesn't show the dark is causing a real problem.

parts.tap: Parents have offered to run a sausage sizzle at every home game to help pay for them.
parts.reason: This shows how lights could be paid for, not why the oval needs them.

parts: Our players are aged from eight to twelve, and we have three teams. The oval also needs new goalposts, but that's a letter for another day. I would be grateful if the council could discuss this at its next meeting. Yours sincerely, Dev Marsh, coach of the Bluster Rock Roos

encounters.frame: The Year 6 debate on canteen food got heated. The Bilbolster took notes with its ears.
encounters.text: On Thursday, Year 6 held a debate about what the canteen should sell. Mo was the timekeeper, although he kept stopping the clock to tell jokes about sausages.
encounters.prompt: Put each claim from the debate in the right box.
encounters.success: Backing must fit the claim and show why. A 'because' with a feeling or an off-topic fact holds nothing up.

bins: backed-up claim: a reason or proof that supports it

items.text: Last term, the fruit cups sold out every single day. The canteen should sell more fruit.
items.reason: Fruit cups selling out shows students would buy more fruit. Backing doesn't need 'because'.

items.text: Fruit is the best snack, because it is better than every other snack.
items.reason: 'Better than every other snack' just means 'best'. The claim holds itself up.

items.text: Chips should stay on the menu, because I'd be really sad without them.
items.reason: Being sad is a feeling. It doesn't show why the canteen should keep chips.

items.text: Sushi rolls would sell well. Sixty students asked for them in the canteen survey.
items.reason: Sixty students asking is proof that sushi would sell. The claim is backed up.

items.text: Salads would sell out every day, because lettuce is mostly water.
items.reason: Lettuce really is mostly water, but that doesn't show kids would buy salads. The reason doesn't fit.

items.text: Pies should stay, because the canteen makes more money from pies than anything else.
items.reason: Making the most money is a real reason to keep pies. The claim is backed up.

items.text: The menu is perfect, because nobody could possibly want to change it.
items.reason: This tells you to agree without showing why. Nothing holds the claim up.

encounters.frame: Wren has written to the council about the dingo rescue centre. The Bilbolster is reading it upside down.
encounters.prompt: Wren claims the rescue centre needs a bigger pen. Tap the sentence that backs up her claim.

encounters.frame: Zed's game review has a weak spot. The Bilbolster found it in about two seconds.
encounters.text: REVIEW: SKY RANCH, by Zed. Sky Ranch is a farming game in which you run a cattle station on a floating island above the outback. You can grow saltbush, herd floating cows and build windmills that keep your island in the air. The game has over 200 different buildings to unlock, and you can visit your friends' islands to trade. The art is gorgeous, with sunsets that turn the whole sky orange and purple. I have played it for thirty hours, and I still find new things every time. My little cousin, who is seven, learned to play it in an afternoon. Sky Ranch costs $25, which is cheaper than most farming games. There is nothing extra to buy once you own it. The music is calm. At the end of my review, I listed three reasons to buy it, but Tully says one of them isn't a reason at all.

encounters.frame: Maxx is answering questions about his trip to the Moon. The Bilbolster's ears keep drooping.
encounters.text: Maxx it out, Vantafam! It's question time, and you've been flooding my comments about the Gold Rocket. Some of you want to know if I'm really going to the Moon. A few of you, and you know who you are, keep asking whether the rocket is just a water tank with gold paint on it. Rude! The launch is now set for 3 March, and tickets to watch from the beach have already sold out. Here are my answers to your four most popular questions, so read them carefully. The rocket is real. Engineers from three countries helped build it, and their names are on the side. The trip is possible, because my rocket has already flown to the edge of space twice, on film. The rocket is safe for the trip, because it has a waterslide, four seats and real gold paint. The Gold Rocket is the fastest rocket on Bluster Rock. In last month's test, it beat the old record. And before you ask, yes, I'm taking my hair spray. Smash that heart button like it owes you money, and I'll see you from space! Stay gold!
encounters.prompt: Which of Maxx's answers is a bare claim?
encounters.success: A waterslide and gold paint are real, but they don't show the rocket is safe. The backing doesn't fit.

options.text: The rocket is real. Engineers from three countries helped build it, and their names are on the side.
options.reason: Engineers' names on the side are something you could check. This claim is backed up.

options.text: The trip is possible, because my rocket has already flown to the edge of space twice, on film.
options.reason: Two filmed flights are proof you could check. This claim is backed up.

options.text: The rocket is safe for the trip, because it has a waterslide, four seats and real gold paint.
The Gold Rocket is the fastest rocket on Bluster Rock. In last month's test, it beat the old record.
options.reason: 'Fastest' sounds like boasting, but a record-beating test is proof. This claim is backed up.

encounters.frame: Slick Vinnie is selling a shampoo for lizards. The Bilbolster has never been so confused.
encounters.prompt: Vinnie makes four claims. Tap the one with nothing really backing it up.
encounters.success: Nice smells don't make scales shine. A 'because' isn't enough: the reason has to fit the claim.

parts: SLICK VINNIE'S SCALE-SHINE: SHAMPOO FOR LIZARDS! Does your blue-tongue look a bit dull? Is your bearded dragon having a bad scale day? Then read on.

parts.tap: Scale-Shine is gentle, because it's made from aloe vera and nothing else.
parts.reason: Being made only from aloe vera is a reason it's gentle. This claim is backed up.

parts.tap: Scale-Shine makes scales shine, because it comes in two smells, eucalyptus and fresh rain.
Scale-Shine works fast. In our test, twenty lizards were shiny after one wash.
parts.reason: Twenty shiny lizards after one wash is proof, with no 'because' needed. This claim is backed up.

encounters.frame: Ada Pennick is drafting a second letter about the turtles. The Bilbolster is reading it from a rock pool.
encounters.text: Dear Editor, Last month, I wrote to object to jet ski hire in Bluster Bay, and many readers have asked me why I am so certain that jet skis are hurting the turtles. It is a fair question. The northern end of the bay has been a nesting beach for green turtles for as long as anyone can remember, and every summer, volunteers like me count the nests, fence them off and watch the hatchlings scramble down to the water. Until this year, injured turtles were rare. Each nest holds around a hundred eggs, and the hatchlings come out at night, guided by the moonlight on the water. Jet skis are allowed in the bay from 7 am to 7 pm, seven days a week, and the hire shop has twelve of them. On a busy Saturday, all twelve are out on the water at once. I am not against fun, and I am not against tourists, who bring welcome money to our town. But I believe that jet skis are hurting the turtles, and I want to show readers why. I have one sentence left to write before I send this letter, and I want it to be the strongest backing I can give. The council will vote on the jet ski hire licence on 12 December. Yours faithfully, Ada Pennick, turtle volunteer
encounters.prompt: Ada claims jet skis are hurting the turtles. Which sentence would back up her claim best?
encounters.success: Propeller cuts since the hire shop opened link the injuries to jet skis. Nothing else shows a turtle was hurt.

options.text: Jet skis are clearly a menace, as anyone with eyes can see.
options.reason: 'As anyone can see' asks you to agree without showing anything. The claim stays bare.

options.text: On one Saturday, locals counted nine jet skis zooming within fifty metres of the nesting beach.
options.reason: Close to the beach isn't the same as hurting turtles. Nothing here shows a turtle was hurt.

options.text: The hire shop earned $60,000 last summer, and it also sponsors Maxx Vantablack's channel.
options.reason: This might make you distrust the shop, but money and sponsors don't show any turtle was hurt.

options.text: Since the hire shop opened, rangers have found fourteen turtles with propeller cuts.

encounters.frame: Maxx is defending his art auction in the comments. The Bilbolster is trying very hard to find any backing.
encounters.text: Maxx it out, Vantafam! Some of you have been leaving comments about my painting, 'Gold on Gold', which was auctioned last night. A few haters are saying it was just a canvas with gold paint splashed on it, and one person said it looked like a dropped pancake. Let me tell you about the painting. It's two metres wide, and it's covered in real gold leaf. I finished it in a single afternoon, between my morning workout and my hair appointment. The auction was held in public at the Bluster Rock town hall, and bidders offered up to $40,000 for it. Thousands of Vantafam watched the bidding live on my stream. I also asked my Goldies to write in, and some of them make excellent points. My Goldie Kaz says it is the best thing I have ever painted, and Kaz has seen everything I've painted. Remember, every cent goes to the Maxx Vantablack Rescue Fund, so if you complain, you're basically complaining about rescued Creatures. That's Maxx-imum content! Stay gold!
encounters.prompt: Maxx claims 'Gold on Gold' is valuable. Which detail backs up that claim best?
encounters.success: Valuable means people will pay a lot for it. Real bids at a public auction are proof you could check.

options.text: Bidders at a public auction offered up to $40,000 for it.
It is two metres wide and covered in real gold leaf.
options.reason: Gold leaf is very thin. Size and gold show what it's made of, not what people would pay.

options.text: Thousands of Vantafam watched the bidding live on his stream.
options.reason: Watching costs nothing. A big audience doesn't show anyone would pay for it.

options.text: Kaz says it is the best thing Maxx has ever painted.
options.reason: Kaz is a fan, and 'best' is a feeling. It doesn't show what the painting is worth.

encounters.frame: A local band has written to the Bluster Rock Bugle. The Bilbolster is tapping its foot and its ears.
encounters.prompt: The band claims a festival would be good for local shops. Tap the sentence that backs up this claim best.
encounters.success: Doubled takings at the last festival is checkable proof about these very shops. The others only hint at it.

parts: Dear Editor, We are Red Dust Static, a band that started in a garage behind the Bluster Rock service station four years ago. We are writing to ask the council to bring back the Bluster Rock Music Festival, which has not been held since 2019. We believe a festival would be good for local shops.

parts.tap: Lots of shop owners have told us they would love to have a festival again.
parts.reason: Wanting a festival shows the owners hope it helps. It doesn't show it did.

parts.tap: Festivals in other towns, like Saltbush Creek, are said to be good for business.
parts.reason: 'Are said to be' means nobody has checked. It's about another town, too.

parts.tap: At the last festival, the bakery, the service station and the newsagent all reported that their takings doubled for the weekend.
Thousands of people came to the last festival, and many said they had a great time.
parts.reason: A big, happy crowd is a good sign, but it doesn't show anyone spent money in the shops.

parts: We would happily play for free, and three other local bands have already offered to join us. We have even found a stage: the old flatbed truck behind the footy club, which only needs new tyres and a very thorough clean. If the council agrees, we could hold the festival next autumn, when the evenings are cool. Yours sincerely, Jojo, Sunny and Dax, Red Dust Static

encounters.frame: Gus is preparing a speech for the school council. The Bilbolster has spotted a reason that isn't one.
encounters.text: For three years, Gus has been asking Bluster Rock Primary to start a robotics club. This term, the school council has finally agreed to listen, and Gus has five minutes to make his case on Thursday. He has borrowed a robot kit from the library for free and built a small robot called Sorty, which sorts recycling into the right bins. Sorty has a camera eye, two claws made from salad tongs and a conveyor belt that used to be part of a treadmill. In a test on the staffroom rubbish bin, Sorty sorted forty-one out of fifty items correctly. It did, however, put a banana skin on Principal Okafor's chair. Gus has heard that the robotics club at Saltbush Creek Primary is very popular. He has also collected names, and twenty-six students have already signed up to join. His speech ends with three reasons, but Wren has pointed out that one of them doesn't give the council a reason to agree. Gus would like to fix it before Thursday, preferably without starting again.
encounters.prompt: Tap the reason that doesn't back up Gus's claim. Then choose the strongest backing to swap in.

encounters.frame: Four companies sent pitches to the Vantamart. The Bilbolster is reading the soap one with its nose held.

parts: A NOTICE FROM SLICK VINNIE, TOUR GUIDE. As you will have read in the Bugle, strange green lights have been appearing above the old mine at the back of Bluster Rock. People have been asking me about them all week, so here is what I can tell you.

parts.reason: Camera footage is proof you could check. This claim is backed up.

The lights appear at the same time each night. They have been seen at about 11:40 pm three nights in a row.
parts.reason: Three sightings at the same time are proof of a pattern. This claim is backed up.
